neighbours.label: a chance-or-room noun right after a verb of having or giving (have the chance, gave them an opening, have time to, no choice, more room to, some leeway, a shot at; also Gelegenheit, возможность, 機會 after a having verb), read on the noun; it fires even when the noun means something else after 'has' ('the shop has an opening for a cashier'); quiet on the same nouns without that verb (as subject, 'by chance', 'what time is it', 'the room was painted') and after 'missed' or 'took'
fire: The shop has an opening for a cashier.
If you have the chance, visit the old harbor at sunset.
The coach gave them an opening to argue their case before the vote.
Do you have time to look over my essay tonight?
We had no choice but to cancel the picnic.
The new layout gives the kids more room to play.
Our manager gave us some leeway on the deadline.
She finally has a shot at the championship this year.
quiet: Her choice of dress surprised everyone.
By chance, we met an old friend at the harbor.
The opening of the new bridge drew a large crowd.
What time is it in Tokyo right now?
The choice of venue was announced yesterday.
The room was painted a pale shade of green.
Leeway in the rules caused some confusion among players.
He missed the chance to visit the harbor at sunset.

predictions: most fire items clear 0.2 (the cashier vacancy item weakest, ~0.25); quiet items near zero
